subject: Carrying forward an unused grouping variable.

messages.author: ddc91303cb21ac62
messages.subject: Carrying forward an unused grouping variable.
parts:
Hello all,

I have quick question about the usage of ddply. If I have two grouping
variables but only take a mean based on one of them (fac2), how can I
add a column that represents the other grouping variable (fac1) to use
simply as a label?


#Here is a simple example
library(plyr)
x <- runif(20,10, 15)
df <- as.data.frame(x)
df$fac1 <- factor(c("Test1","Test1","Test1","Test1","Test1",
"Test2","Test2","Test2","Test2","Test2",
"Test3","Test3","Test3","Test3","Test3",
"Test4","Test4","Test4","Test4","Test4"))

df$fac2 <- factor(c("A","A","B","B"))

#Taking the average based on "fac2"
df.avg <- ddply(df, c("fac2"), function(df) return(c(x.tmp=mean(df
$x))))

#Two columns but I would like to add the third as a label
df

Thanks so much in advance.

Sam
